_port_note: ONE authored card replaces a per-customer factory. The id no longer carries the customer id because the LATCH does: latch_key entity means each account gets its own brake, which is what the namespaced ids were emulating. The factory's build-time option omission becomes locked-visible per §3.3 — see _behaviour_change. Tagged critical: the account is in Risk with a churn countdown running, so the decision has a deadline and cannot wait on a weighted draw. This is the behaviour _maybe_enqueue_retention had before it was retired. TICK CORRECTED TO signal. The old sweep fired on the EDGE — inside the branch that moves an account INTO Risk — and a `tick: daily` port turned that edge into a state, which asks again every draw for as long as the account is dying. `customer_health_changed` is the edge, emitted by CustomerRegistry.set_lifecycle_phase, and it carries the customer id, so the slot is bound by the emitter rather than guessed by a selector. The cooldown is ONE day, not twenty-one: the Sales tab's İlgilen button re-opens the same card, and the factory's own comment said the player may reopen before expiry and still rescue. What one day forbids is re-opening the card you just answered, which is an undo, not a decision. COPY LIE FIXED: the discount option carried `add_reputation: +1`. B2BConstants.RETAIN_DISCOUNT_REP is -1 and always was — buying an account back with price costs standing. The port had transcribed the sign of the PROMISE row onto the discount row, which would have shown the player a positive chip for a negative outcome. LOCKS ADDED. The old builders withheld these rows by not BUILDING them — the promise row was skipped when a word was already open, the discount row when the cap was spent. A card is data now, so the row exists and must lock instead, which is §17.5's ruling and the better behaviour: a row that disappears teaches the player nothing, a row that is greyed with its reason teaches them the rule. Ported without them, every request card would have minted unlimited promises and uncapped discounts through a channel the retention card had closed.
_behaviour_change: The 'promise it' row was ABSENT when there was nothing left to promise. §3.3 is explicit that a locked option is shown greyed with its reason and never hidden, so it is now visible-and-locked. The player learns the row exists and why they cannot take it, instead of a card that quietly has three options one day and four the next.

condition.reason: the account is not in Risk with a countdown running

_r8a_note: A non-critical interrupt is demotable (§13.2), and a demoted card lands on the desk with a clock — which is the only reason paper is a safe floor for I4. So it carries the paper trio even though it usually renders as an interrupt.
